text_blocks.snippet: Diagnosis of acute glomerulonephritis involves a combination of clinical evaluation, blood and urine tests, and sometimes kidney biopsy. It's often discovered due to symptoms like blood in the urine, facial puffiness, and high blood pressure, which can arise suddenly or after an infection.

list.title: Urinalysis:
list.snippet: This test checks for the presence of blood and protein in the urine, which are common indicators of glomerulonephritis. Red blood cell casts, if present, are virtually diagnostic of active glomerular inflammation.

list.title: Blood Tests:
list.snippet: Blood tests measure waste product levels (like creatinine and urea nitrogen) to assess kidney function. They can also detect abnormal antibodies or signs of infection.
